ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the square $ABCD$, $E$ is a point on the diagonal $BD$, and $BE=BC$, then what is the value of $\angle DCE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a square, \\
$\therefore \angle CBE=45^\circ$, $\angle BCD=90^\circ$, \\
Since BE=BC, \\
$\therefore \angle BCE= \frac{1}{2} \times (180^\circ-45^\circ)=67.5^\circ$, \\
Therefore, $\angle DCE=\angle BCD-\angle BCE=90^\circ-67.5^\circ=\boxed{22.5^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates and slopes. From the image, read the orientation of the square: take C as the top-right corner, D to its left, B directly below it, and E on diagonal BD with CE drawn. From the text, impose that the side length BC equals BE. Set the square side length to 1 with coordinates C = (0,0), D = (-1,0), B = (0,-1). The diagonal from B to D has direction (-1,1), so the unit direction from B toward D is (-1/sqrt(2), 1/sqrt(2)). Since BE = BC = 1, E = B + 1·(-1/sqrt(2), 1/sqrt(2)) = (-1/sqrt(2), -1 + 1/sqrt(2)). Then vector CE is (-1/sqrt(2), -1 + 1/sqrt(2)), while CD is horizontal to the left. The angle between CE and CD has tangent equal to vertical drop divided by horizontal leftward run: (1 - 1/sqrt(2))/(1/sqrt(2)) = sqrt(2) - 1. Since tan 22.5° = sqrt(2) - 1, angle DCE = 22.5°.
